title: Halves and Fourths: Equal Parts
standard_text: 1.6G partition two-dimensional figures into two and four fair shares or equal parts and describe the parts using words; 1.6H identify examples and non-examples of halves and fourths
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 halves and fourths worksheets for Texas TEKS 1.6G and 1.6H: equal parts, examples and non-examples, shaded parts and sharing stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Halves are 2 equal parts; fourths are 4 equal parts.
key_sub: A fourth is smaller than a half.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Halves: 2 equal parts. Each part is one half.
  • Fourths (quarters): 4 equal parts. Each part is one fourth.
  • The parts must be the same size.
  • More equal parts means smaller parts: a fourth is smaller than a half.

Examples

Example

A pizza cut into 4 equal parts

4 equal parts

Answer: fourths

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling unequal parts halvesHalves must be the same size.
Counting parts that are not equalCheck that each part is the same size.
Thinking a fourth is bigger than a halfMore parts means smaller parts.

Which is bigger, a half or a fourth of the same pizza?

items.e: There are 2 equal shares. 2 equal shares are halves.

items.e: There are 4 equal shares, so they are fourths, not halves. There are 2 lines, but 4 shares. Count the shares.

items.q: The rectangle is cut into halves. Which words name the whole rectangle?
items.e: The rectangle has 2 equal shares. Each one is a half. The whole is two halves.

items.q: What do we call 2 equal shares?
items.e: 2 equal shares are called halves. We do not say twos.

items.q: How many halves make a whole?
items.e: A whole cut into halves has 2 equal shares. 2 halves make a whole.

items.q: A circle is cut into halves. How many equal shares are there?
items.e: Halves means 2 equal shares.

items.q: A circle is cut into 2 equal shares. What is each share?
items.e: 2 equal shares are halves. Each share is half of the circle.

items.q: One straight cut goes down the middle of a square. How many equal shares are there?
items.e: 1 cut makes 2 shares. The cut is in the middle, so the shares are equal. They are halves.

items.q: A shape has 2 pieces. One piece is big. One piece is small. Are they halves?
items.e: Halves must be the same size. A big piece and a small piece are not halves.

items.q: Ella cuts a cookie in half. How many pieces does she have?
items.e: Cutting in half makes 2 equal pieces. Each piece is half of the cookie.

items.q: Max cuts a pancake into halves. He eats one half. How much is left?
items.e: The whole pancake is 2 halves. Max eats 1 half, so 1 half is left.

items.q: Which is not a way to cut a rectangle in half?
items.e: A cut near one end makes a big piece and a small piece. The other cuts make 2 equal shares.

items.e: There are 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths. Count the shares, not the 2 lines.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into fourths?
items.e: There are 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths. Count the shares, not the 3 lines.

items.q: This square has 2 lines. How many equal shares does it have?
items.e: Count the shares, not the lines. 2 lines cross and make 4 equal shares. They are fourths.

items.q: What do we call 4 equal shares?
items.e: 4 equal shares are called fourths. They are also called quarters.

items.q: What is another name for a fourth?
items.e: A fourth is also called a quarter. Both mean 1 of 4 equal shares.

items.q: Which is bigger: a fourth of a pizza or a quarter of the same pizza?
items.e: A fourth and a quarter are the same. Both are 1 of 4 equal shares of the pizza.

items.q: How many fourths make a whole?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal shares. 4 fourths make a whole.

items.q: How many quarters make a whole?
items.e: Quarters are 4 equal shares. 4 quarters make a whole.

items.q: A square is cut into 4 equal shares. What is each share?
items.e: 4 equal shares are quarters. Each share is a quarter of the square.

items.q: Ana cuts a waffle into fourths. How many pieces does she have?
items.e: Fourths means 4 equal pieces.

items.q: Sam cuts a cake into 4 pieces. One piece is much bigger. Are they fourths?
items.e: Fourths must be 4 equal shares. Sam has 4 pieces, but they are not the same size.

items.q: Is this circle cut into equal shares? How many?
items.e: There are 4 pieces, but they are not the same size. Some pieces are bigger. So they are not equal shares.

items.q: Is this rectangle cut into equal shares? How many?

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one half of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 2 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one half of the rectangle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 2 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one half of the rectangle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the square is shaded?
items.e: The square has 2 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one half of the square is shaded.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 2 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one half of the circle is shaded.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 4 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one fourth of the circle is shaded. Count all 4 shares, not only the white ones.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal shares. 1 share is shaded. So one fourth of the rectangle is shaded. Count all 4 shares, not only the white ones.

items.q: Which shape has one half shaded?
items.e: Shape D has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a half is shaded. The shares must be equal, and only 1 of 2 is shaded.

items.q: Which shape has one half shaded?
items.e: Shape A has 2 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a half is shaded. The shares must be equal, and only 1 of 2 is shaded.

items.q: Which shape has one fourth shaded?
items.e: Shape A has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a fourth is shaded. The shares must be equal, and only 1 of 4 is shaded.

items.q: Which shape has one fourth shaded?
items.e: Shape D has 4 equal shares and 1 is shaded, so a fourth is shaded. The shares must be equal, and only 1 of 4 is shaded.

items.q: The rectangle is cut into fourths. Which words name the whole rectangle?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 equal shares. The whole is four fourths. (It has 2 lines, but 4 shares.)

items.q: The circle is cut into quarters. Which words name the whole circle?
items.e: The circle has 4 equal shares. The whole is four quarters.

items.q: What part of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: Both halves are shaded. 2 halves make the whole rectangle.

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: All 4 fourths are shaded. 4 fourths make the whole circle.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole square?
items.e: The whole square is 4 fourths. 1 is shaded. 1 + 3 = 4, so 3 more must be shaded.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into halves. B is cut into fourths. A half is bigger than a fourth, so A is bigger. (4 is more than 2, but more shares means smaller shares.)

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into fourths. B is cut into halves. A half is bigger than a fourth, so B is bigger.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into fourths. Each shaded share is a fourth of the same square. A triangle and a small square can be the same size.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into halves. Half of a square is the same size, whether the cut goes down the middle or corner to corner.

items.q: The circles are the same size. Which circle has the smallest shares?
items.e: Circle B is cut into fourths. That is the most shares. More shares means smaller shares.

items.q: The rectangles are the same size. Which rectangle has the biggest shares?
items.e: Rectangle A is cut into halves. The others are cut into fourths. Fewer shares means bigger shares.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of a pizza or a fourth of the same pizza?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal shares. A fourth is 1 of 4 equal shares. More shares means smaller shares. So half is bigger.

items.q: Which is smaller: a quarter of a cake or half of the same cake?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 shares. Half is 1 of 2 shares. 4 shares are smaller, so a quarter is smaller.

items.q: You cut the same pie into more equal shares. What happens to each share?
items.e: The pie stays the same. More shares means each share is smaller.

items.q: Mia cuts her pancake into halves. Ben cuts the same size pancake into fourths. Whose pieces are bigger?
items.e: Ben has more pieces, so his pieces are smaller. Halves are bigger than fourths, so Mia’s pieces are bigger.

items.q: Ava shares a sandwich fairly with 3 friends. What share does each person get?
items.e: Ava and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal shares are fourths. Do not forget to count Ava.

items.q: Leo and his sister share a pizza fairly. What share does each one get?
items.e: Leo and his sister are 2 people. 2 equal shares are halves. Each one gets a half.

items.q: Four kids share a big cookie fairly. What share does each kid get?
items.e: Four kids means 4 equal shares. Each kid gets a quarter (a fourth) of the cookie.

items.q: Nora folds a paper in half. Then she opens it. How many equal shares does she see?
items.e: One fold makes 2 equal shares: 2 halves. The fold is 1 line, but it makes 2 shares.

items.q: Kai folds a square paper in half. He folds it in half again the other way. He opens it. What are the shares?
items.e: The 2 folds cross and make 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths.

items.q: Owen cuts a sandwich into 2 pieces. One is big and one is small. Did he cut it in half?
items.e: Halves must be the same size. A big piece and a small piece are not halves.

items.q: Ella gets half of an apple. Max gets a fourth of the same size apple. Who gets more?
items.e: Half is bigger than a fourth. So Ella gets more apple.

items.q: Omar is very hungry. Should he take half of a pie or a quarter of the same pie?
items.e: Half of a pie is bigger than a quarter of the same pie. Omar should take half.

items.q: Grace eats 2 halves of an orange. How much of the orange does she eat?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Grace eats the whole orange.

items.q: Lily cuts a square cake with 2 cuts. The cuts cross in the middle. How many equal shares are there?
items.e: 2 cuts that cross in the middle make 4 equal shares. Count the shares, not the cuts.
